name: Slowing speech and pausing
lead: Slowing speech and pausing is a delivery technique in which a person speaks at a measured pace and uses deliberate silences to come across as calm, confident and authoritative. People use it to improve how they are perceived in presence and voice rather than in physical features.
Classical rhetoric counts delivery as one of the canons, and describes it as including tone of voice, changes in pace, pauses and volume.[1]

chain: Perceived as calmer and more authoritative
angle.text: Speaking slowly and pausing is used to project calm authority, adding to overall presence alongside appearance.

paras: The technique uses unhurried pacing, pauses before and after key points, and steady breath. Public-speaking references list pace and pauses among elements of delivery, along with tone, volume and body language.[1] Demosthenes is said to have practiced speaking while running to build breath control.[1]
It is discussed under voice and charisma as part of authority delivery.

card.summary: Speaking slowly with deliberate pauses to sound calm, confident and authoritative.

quick.overview:
This is a delivery habit: slow the pace of speech and let pauses do the work.

People use it to sound more composed and authoritative.
quick.mechanism: Slower pacing and silences give words emphasis and signal calm, an element of delivery in classical rhetoric.
quick.risks: No physical risks. Overdoing pauses can feel stilted.
